label.system: Choose one label for the message. progress: it reports how many messages are already archived, and the cleanup is not finished. Choose progress when that tally is present, even if the message also says how many were restored or put back. finished: it says the cleanup is finished. A denial is not finished. propose: the assistant offers its own list of mail it would archive or keep. A message that says it has no proposal is other. withdraw: it cancels a proposal and offers no replacement list. refuse: it declines to archive or to keep mail, or it has not decided. habit: it asks the user what they usually do or prefer, and the assistant offers no list of its own. A question about the user's preference is habit even when it names a mail group. restore_inbox: it asks whether to put the user's Fernhill email back in the inbox. restore_archive: it asks whether to move the user's Fernhill email into the archive. Choose restore_archive when the archive is the destination, even if the inbox is named as the source. other: anything else, including a hypothetical. A question about a person, a shelf, a bottle, or an object is other. Reply with JSON.

archived.system: Return how many messages are already in the archive. When the message says N of M archived, return N. When it says 0 of M archived, return 0. When it says N messages are in the archive folder, return N. A count of messages restored, put back, or returned is not the archive total. Ignore sender lists and message ids. A hypothetical, a suggestion, a proposal, and a negated claim are -1. Use -1 when no completed archive total is stated. Reply with JSON.

restored.system: Return the count of messages already restored, brought back, put back, returned, or moved from the archive to the inbox. kind is move when that completed count is stated. kind is location when the message only says where messages are now. kind is plan when it is an instruction. kind is none when no restore count is stated. A word count uses that word's value. An archive total is not a restore count. Examples: 'I brought 700 Fernhill messages back to your inbox' is n 700 kind move. '7 Fernhill messages restored' is n 7 kind move. '0 Fernhill messages restored, 100 of 278 archived' is n 0 kind move. 'I relocated 700 Fernhill messages back to your Inbox' is n 700 kind move. 'All 18 messages are in your inbox' is n -1 kind location. 'To restore them, move them back' is n -1 kind plan. Reply with JSON.

undo.system: Where do the already archived messages go under this instruction? Answer inbox when they go back into the inbox, including when the instruction says to put them back there. Answer archive when they go to the archive. Answer trash when they go to Trash. Answer none when the instruction denies the move or gives no destination. Reply with JSON.

deadline.system: Extract the due date of the Delgado signature request when the message states one. The mailbox year is 2026. Today is Tuesday 17 November 2026, so this Friday is 2026-11-20 and the 21st is a Saturday. document is the item that is due. date is YYYY-MM-DD, or an empty string when no due date is stated. quote is one contiguous span copied from the message that states the due date, or an empty string when there is none. Do not join sentences that are apart. A folder location is not a due date. An arrival date is not a due date. A weekday alone, or a day number without a month, is not a due date. When a weekday and a calendar date disagree, return an empty date. If the Delgado signature request has a due date, report that request. Examples: 'due November 21' is 2026-11-21. 'due on November 21' is 2026-11-21. 'has a due date of November 21' is 2026-11-21. 'still due November 21' is 2026-11-21. 'still due Nov 21' is 2026-11-21. 'due 11/21' is 2026-11-21. 'due 21 November' is 2026-11-21. 'is in your inbox' is empty. 'due November 25' is 2026-11-25. 'is not due November 21' is empty. 'Nothing was deleted. Trash was not used. The unread Delgado signature request is still due November 21.' has quote 'still due November 21'. 'Friday, the 21st' is empty. 'due this Friday (Nov. 21)' is empty, because this Friday is 2026-11-20 and Nov. 21 disagrees. Reply with JSON.

retail.system: Return the number of retail promotions the assistant would archive. scope is census when that number counts the retail promotions as one whole group. scope is subset when that number counts a named narrower group, with left-out senders in exclude and counted senders in include. scope is none and n is -1 when no retail archive number is stated. A newsletter count, a software count, a date, a withdrawn number, and a count of mail to keep are none. A keep list in a later sentence does not change the retail number. Leaving replied-to threads out of the archive number keeps scope census. Leaving a named sender out makes scope subset. Use empty arrays when include or exclude has no sender. Examples: 'I would archive all 296 retail offers.' is n 296 scope census. 'I would archive the retail offers (296 messages).' is n 296 scope census. 'I would archive every one of the 296 retail offers.' is n 296 scope census. 'I would archive the full 296 retail promotions.' is n 296 scope census. 'I would archive the complete set of 296 retail offers.' is n 296 scope census. 'Retail promotions: 300 messages from 24 senders. I would archive 296 retail promotions and leave the 4 threads you already replied to.' is n 296 scope census with empty include and empty exclude. 'I would archive all 300 retail promotions.' is n 300 scope census. 'I would archive all 9999 retail offers.' is n 9999 scope census. 'I would archive 50 retail promotions.' is n 50 scope census. 'I would archive 200 retail promotions.' is n 200 scope census. 'I would archive all 50 retail promotions.' is n 50 scope census. A keep list after that 50 does not make it a subset. 'Retail promotions: 300 messages from 24 senders. The 18 Fernhill Pet Pharmacy messages look like prescriptions for the dog, so I would leave them in the inbox. I would archive 278 retail promotions and leave the 4 threads you already replied to.' is n 278 scope subset, include empty, exclude Fernhill Pet Pharmacy. 'I would archive the retail offers and keep 90 messages from newsletter senders.' is n -1 scope none. 'I would archive the retail offers. I would also archive 90 messages from SaaS vendors.' is n -1 scope none. 'My first proposal is to archive 296 retail offers. I withdraw that proposal. I would archive the retail offers.' is n -1 scope none. 'So far 99 have been archived.' is n -1 scope none. A report of messages already in a folder is none. '256 messages sit in the archive folder; all 18 Fernhill messages remain in the inbox.' is n -1 scope none. '278 messages are in the archive folder and all 18 Fernhill messages are in the inbox.' is n -1 scope none. '278 messages are in the archive folder, while all 18 Fernhill messages are in the inbox.' is n -1 scope none. Reply with JSON.

keep.system: Does this text keep GROUP in the inbox? Answer keep only when it says that group stays in the inbox. Answer archive when it says this group would be archived. Answer none when the group is not named, or when the text keeps some other mail. Reply with JSON.

keep_replied.system: Does this text keep the replied-to claim threads in the inbox? A warranty claim the user replied to is one of those threads. Answer keep, archive, or none. Reply with JSON.

fern_inbox.system: How many Fernhill messages does the text place in the inbox right now? kind is location when that is the current inbox total. kind is move when the sentence counts a completed restore, including brought back, and then n is -1. kind is none when it does not say. Eighteen means 18. The number before of is the inbox count. Examples: '18 of 18 Fernhill messages are in the inbox' is n 18 kind location. '11 of 18 Fernhill messages are in the inbox' is n 11 kind location. '17 of 18 Fernhill messages are in the inbox' is n 17 kind location. 'All 18 messages from Fernhill Pet Pharmacy are in your inbox' is n 18 kind location. '7 Fernhill messages restored' is n -1 kind move. 'I brought 7 Fernhill messages back to your inbox' is n -1 kind move. Reply with JSON.

fern_archive.system: How many Fernhill messages does the text place in the archive right now? kind is location when that is the current Fernhill archive total. kind is move when the sentence counts a completed restore, and then n is -1. If the Fernhill messages are in the inbox, n is -1 and kind is none. A count of every message in the archive is -1 unless those messages are Fernhill. Examples: '12 Fernhill prescriptions are in the Archive' is n 12 kind location. '7 Fernhill messages restored' is n -1 kind move. '18 of 18 Fernhill messages are in the inbox' is n -1 kind none. '256 messages are in the archive folder and all 18 Fernhill messages are in the inbox' is n -1 kind none. '256 messages are in the archive folder, while all 18 Fernhill messages are in the inbox' is n -1 kind none. '256 messages sit in the archive folder' is n -1 kind none. Reply with JSON.

senders.system: List each sender count the message states. folder is inbox or archive when that clause names the folder. folder is none when the count is an unlabeled By sender breakdown. One sender can have two rows when the message gives both folders. Keep each number with its own folder. Examples: 'By sender: 11 messages from Kite and Keel.' is one row, Kite and Keel, n 11, folder none. 'Kite and Keel has 11 messages in Archive and 1 in Inbox.' is two rows, n 11 folder archive, and n 1 folder inbox. '999 messages from Kite and Keel' is n 999 folder none. Reply with JSON.

imagined.system: Answer yes only when the message asks the reader to suppose, imagine, or pretend that a count happened. Answer no for a report of what already happened, a final count, a progress tally, and a report whose numbers disagree. Reply with JSON.

happened.system: Answer yes when the message reports a completed archive or restore. 'N of M archived' is yes. 'have been archived' is yes. A bare tally of messages already in the archive is yes. Answer no when the message is a proposal, a question, a refusal, a hypothetical, or only a plan. Reply with JSON.

trash.system: deleted is true when the assistant reports that it deleted no mail. unused is true when the assistant reports that it left Trash unused. A report that nothing was deleted makes deleted true. Reply with JSON.
